vulkanSdk.name: vulkansdk-windows-X64-1.4.357.0.exe
vulkanSdk.use: Build-time only: Vulkan headers, the vulkan-1 import library and glslc for ggml-vulkan's shaders. Nothing from the SDK is bundled; vulkan-1.dll comes from the user's GPU driver.

provenanceNotes: whisper.cpp is the runtime behind Buzz, Vibe, Speech Note and Whispering; its Vulkan backend covers NVIDIA, AMD and Intel GPUs, including integrated ones, and its CPU backend covers every x64 PC.

The x64 DLLs are built on a GitHub windows-2022 runner from the pinned commit, which the build verifies with git rev-parse, using the MSVC toolset of that image and the shared Visual C++ runtime the app already bundles. GGML_BACKEND_DL keeps the Vulkan backend a separately loaded DLL, so a PC without a Vulkan driver loads the CPU backend instead of failing to start.
OpenMP is off so no vcomp140.dll is needed; ggml's own thread pool runs the CPU backend.

The Vulkan SDK installer is pinned by URL, byte count and the SHA-256 LunarG publishes (https://vulkan.lunarg.com/sdk/sha/1.4.357.0/windows/vulkansdk-windows-X64-1.4.357.0.exe.json), which matched the downloaded bytes on 2026-09-23.

The ARM64 DLLs are built natively on a GitHub windows-11-arm runner inside that image's Visual Studio ARM64 developer environment. ggml refuses MSVC for ARM ("MSVC is not supported for ARM, use clang"), so the image's clang targets arm64-pc-windows-msvc with Ninja, following upstream's cmake/arm64-windows-llvm.cmake, and links the same shared Visual C++ runtime.

ARM64 is CPU only. GGML_CPU_ALL_VARIANTS stops with "Unsupported ARM target OS" for Windows in this ggml, so ARM64 ships one ggml-cpu.dll instead of run-time selected variants. GGML_CPU_ARM_ARCH=armv8-a keeps it to the base ARMv8-A instruction set every Windows ARM64 PC runs; upstream's toolchain file uses armv8.7-a and fast floating-point math, which would stop older PCs and change numerics. No Vulkan backend is built: upstream publishes Windows ARM64 CPU, OpenCL (Adreno) and CUDA builds but no Vulkan build, LunarG's ARM64 SDK (https://vulkan.lunarg.com/sdk/sha/1.4.357.0/warm/vulkansdk-windows-ARM64-1.4.357.0.exe.json) is not pinned here, and the hosted ARM64 runners have no GPU to test one.

Output DLL hashes depend on the runner's compiler, so each build records them in runtime-manifest.json with the compiler version; the bundle and package authenticate the DLLs against that manifest and the manifest's pins against this file.
